topic: calibrated local Gibbs prediction and experimental purity readout

claims.exact_statement: For finite Hermitian K,L with ||K-L||<=kappa, normalized Gibbs states satisfy T(rho_K,rho_L)<=tanh(kappa/2). If each prepared tau is within trace distance epsilon_prep of the actual Gibbs state, then every reduced state obeys ||tau_S-rho_0,S||_1<=2(epsilon_prep+tanh(kappa/2)).
assumptions: Finite dimension; Gibbs exponentials of finite Hermitian matrices.
A valid bound on the global exponent difference and per-copy preparation error is supplied.
claims.status: Internally reconstructed finite-dimensional proof; also present in the N90 audit. No external specialist review or formal proof checker.
claims.proof_path: work/agents/materials_energy/manybody_certification/CYCLE2_REPORT.md, sections 'Model and calibration interface' and 'Robustness lemma and end-to-end bounds'; work/agents/materials_energy/manybody_certification/astra/source_pages/d-6850ae0710b7f495.txt:195-208.
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard Gibbs continuity/data-processing mechanism; no novelty claim.
costs: Hamiltonian/temperature calibration must supply a global exponent bound.
Preparation error is experimental input; no thermalization time is proved.
claims.falsifier: A local trace-distance confidence interval outside the bound under independently valid finite-model calibration/preparation assumptions.
claims.next_gate: Prove a local-marginal robustness theorem under extensive local coefficient errors with explicit assumptions.

claims.exact_statement: Conditional on the homogeneous Chen-Liu coefficient FPRAS and N90 reduction, a rational finite easy-plane XXZ model in the stated cone admits a classical predictor for any specified k=O(log n) RDM to trace-norm error epsilon_M, with runtime polynomial in input bit length, n, numerical beta C, 4^k, 1/epsilon_M, and log(1/delta_M).
assumptions: Loopless finite graph; rational alpha>=|gamma|, b>=0, arbitrary rational c.
Chen-Liu homogeneous counting theorem and rational-bit implementation are correct and available.
claims.status: Source-derived conditional candidate; N90 reduction internally audited but not externally proof-certified; FPRAS execution unimplemented; priority unresolved.
claims.novelty_boundary: Theorem 5.1 and rational Remark A.4 are imported; N90 reduction is a candidate consequence, not a new counting theorem or priority claim.
costs: Runtime is polynomial in numerical beta C, not only its bit length.
No global quantum Gibbs preparation, coefficient acquisition, or nature validation.
claims.falsifier: An independently checked finite instance whose exact RDM falls outside the claimed predictor interval.
claims.next_gate: Implement the counting chain on explicit lifted instances and obtain independent specialist audit of the reduction.

claims.exact_statement: Under the predictor, calibration, and iid preparation assumptions, a norm-one local observable estimated from N single-copy measurements has residual from the N90 prediction at most sqrt(2 log(2/delta_E)/N)+epsilon_M+2(epsilon_prep+tanh(kappa/2)), with failure probability at most delta_E+delta_M. Full Pauli tomography with M=4^k-1 strings and m shots per string has raw trace-norm radius sqrt(2 M log(2M/delta_E)/m).
assumptions: Predictor RDM trace-norm error epsilon_M except with probability delta_M.
Prepared copies are iid in tau with T(tau,rho_*)<=epsilon_prep.
The observable norm is at most one; tomography allocates m copies to each nonidentity Pauli.
claims.status: Derived by composing the Gibbs continuity lemma, Hoeffding, Pauli orthogonality, and the conditional N90 predictor; no device experiment run.
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard statistical/norm inequalities packaged for the N90 interface; no novelty claim.
costs: One system copy per targeted Pauli shot.
Uniform tomography sufficient count is 2(4^k-1)^2 epsilon_T^-2 log(2(4^k-1)/delta_E) for raw trace-norm radius epsilon_T.
claims.falsifier: A pre-registered local Pauli residual outside the total statistical, predictor, calibration, and preparation radius.
claims.next_gate: Test on a finite simulator after acquiring coefficient, omitted-term, and preparation bounds.

claims.exact_statement: For q>=2, the real cyclic-permutation measurement on q iid copies has mean p_q=Tr(tau_S^q), outcomes in [-1,1], and additive radius sqrt(2 log(2/delta_E)/r) after r groups using q r system copies. Relative error epsilon has sufficient count 2q log(2/delta_E)/(epsilon^2 p_q^2), and p_q>=d^(1-q) gives worst-case sufficient count 2q d^(2(q-1)) epsilon^-2 log(2/delta_E). Comparing with the N90 RDM prediction adds q epsilon_M+2q(epsilon_prep+tanh(kappa/2)); the N97 relative model predictor can reduce model-side error but not laboratory variance.
assumptions: Controlled cyclic permutation/ancilla readout or equivalent is physically implementable.
claims.status: Measurement identity and concentration derived; SWAP/Renyi measurement is established prior art; no device execution or minimax lower bound claimed.
claims.novelty_boundary: Cyclic-permutation/SWAP is prior art. N97 avoids inverse purity only for classical model-side counting; comparison applies to specified estimators, not a minimax lower bound.
costs: Controlled q-cycle, ancilla, synchronization, readout, and thermalization time are platform costs not established by the model.
Relative physical estimation has inverse-purity dependence.
claims.falsifier: A finite-dimensional identity mismatch or iid multi-copy data outside the stated confidence interval beyond its allocated failure probability.
claims.next_gate: Benchmark q=2 on a simulator while recording preparation, controlled-SWAP, readout, and drift costs.

claims.exact_statement: For bounded-degree graphs with O(n) local terms and fixed per-term coefficient error u, the only proved global-norm route has exponent error O(beta n u), becoming uninformative with n. No local-marginal stability theorem under this extensive budget is proved. N52 does not close the gap without its missing local-to-central weighted-L2 premise.
assumptions: Only coefficient intervals and global operator-norm Gibbs continuity are used.
No clustering or high-temperature response assumption is supplied.
claims.status: UNKNOWN for actual local robustness; explicit limitation of this proof route.
claims.novelty_boundary: Does not assert local Gibbs states are actually unstable; only the current global-norm proof loses control.
costs: For fixed global tolerance, this route requires aggregate calibration precision scaling as 1/n.
claims.falsifier: A local continuity theorem under explicit finite-range/clustering assumptions closes this proof gap; a family with order-one local response to fixed local errors would show why stronger assumptions are needed.
claims.next_gate: Derive or refute a local response bound with explicit beta, degree, correlation-length, and perturbation dependence.

claims.exact_statement: For the four-site path fixture alpha=1, gamma=1/2, b=1/4, c=(1/10,-3/20,1/5,-1/10), beta=0.7, dense double-precision diagonalization gives Tr(X1X2 rho_12)=0.47024547 and Tr(rho_12^2)=0.39719966. Under ||E||<=0.01, epsilon_prep=0.003, epsilon_M=0.002, at B=211934 and delta_E=delta_M=0.01, the CYCLE2 radii are about 0.0221 for targeted X1X2, 0.1454 for the uniform-tomography RDM, and 0.0400 for q=2 purity.
assumptions: Numbers are NumPy double-precision calculations, not exact rational evaluation.
Error/preparation budgets are hypothetical, not measured device data.
claims.status: Finite numerical model check only; no experiment and no N90 algorithm execution.
claims.novelty_boundary: Small sanity benchmark; no novelty or material-system claim.
costs: Shot budget excludes thermalization and coherent q=2 gate costs.
claims.falsifier: Re-running the saved script with materially different outputs indicates a numerical or transcription error; it does not falsify the asymptotic theorem.
claims.next_gate: Keep as a finite fixture; replace with a larger simulator/material run only after calibration and preparation bounds are measured.

assumptions: Priority statement limited to the linked primary papers.
claims.novelty_boundary: The lab observable is not new; N97's relative guarantee is conditional and applies to model-side classical counting only.
costs: Replicated states and permutation/switch operations; hardware cost is platform-dependent.
